question.text: How many confirmed measles cases will Wisconsin DHS report for 2026 as of November 27, 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the headline statewide figure for measles in Wisconsin in 2026 printed on the Wisconsin Department of Health Services (DHS) "Outbreaks, Recalls, and Investigations" page (https://www.dhs.wisconsin.gov/outbreaks/index.htm) in the most recent version of that page available at 23:59 UTC on November 27, 2026. The resolution value is the number N in DHS's headline sentence ("As of [date], the Wisconsin Department of Health Services (DHS) has confirmed N cases of measles in Wisconsin ... in 2026"), used exactly as DHS publishes it, with no adjustment for case classification. For example, a headline reading "has confirmed 738 cases of measles in Wisconsin" resolves to 738, even if a sub-total elsewhere on the page reads "370 confirmed and 6 probable". County-level figures and the Southwest Wisconsin outbreak sub-total are never used. The "as of" date printed with the headline is irrelevant: whatever headline figure is displayed on the page at that moment is the answer, including if DHS has not posted a new update since November 24, 2026.
question.fine_print: If the measles section has been moved off the outbreaks page, the statewide total 2026 case count shown in DHS's measles data dashboard at https://www.dhs.wisconsin.gov/immunization/measles.htm is used, exactly as displayed there and again without subtracting probable cases. If the outbreaks page cannot be reached and no archived copy of that page from November 27, 2026 exists (e.g., via the Internet Archive), or if no statewide 2026 case total is displayed on either page, the question is annulled.

## Wisconsin measles: 2026 statewide count, research as of Nov 17, 2026

**Key points**
- The resolution page still shows **651 cases (as of Nov 13)**.
- The Nov 10 to Nov 13 rise was **33 cases a day**, the fastest yet.
- I found no Tuesday Nov 17 update yet.
- The figure displayed at 23:59 UTC Nov 27 could come from either the **Tue Nov 24 or Fri Nov 27 update**, depending on whether Friday's goes up on time.

### 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-17 (fetched today): the headline reads "Measles cases in Wisconsin - Updated November 13, 2026 … As of November 13, [DHS] has confirmed **651 cases** of measles in Wisconsin, 14 hospitalizations, and two deaths in 2026." [DHS outbreaks page](https://www.dhs.wisconsin.gov/outbreaks/index.htm)
- The county table on that page (cases from Aug 1 to Nov 13) adds up to **649**:
  - Grant 222, Lafayette 122 (6 of them probable), Iowa 97, Columbia 47, Chippewa 45, Jackson 45 (25 probable), Green Lake 14, Vernon 14, Sauk 11, Marquette 10, Marathon 6, Rock 5 (all probable), Clark 4, and seven counties with 1 each.
  - Marathon, Richland and Rock are marked as more than 21 days since the last rash onset.
  - The other 2 cases in the headline seem to be Dane and Waukesha cases from before August. [WIZM](https://www.wizmnews.com/2026/11/13/measles-case-reported-in-monroe-county-wi-at-551-cases/)
- The [measles dashboard page](https://www.dhs.wisconsin.gov/immunization/measles.htm) says data are updated twice a week and counts include confirmed plus probable cases. Its numbers sit in an embedded dashboard that I could not read.
- I found no CSV or JSON data file behind the page.

### 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet.
- There are 10 days to go, with probably 3 to 4 updates: Tue Nov 17, Fri Nov 20, Tue Nov 24 and Fri Nov 27.
- Posting lag matters. The Nov 6 data appeared on the page around Nov 9, while the Nov 13 data was posted the same day.

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-17: PAHO announced the US has lost its measles elimination status. [El Nuevo Diario](https://elnuevodiario.com.do/estados-unidos-pierde-la-certificacion-de-pais-libre-de-sarampion-tras-diez-muertes/)
- 2026-11-16: A Green Bay hospital (Bellin) is preparing for possible measles patients and cited DHS's figure of 649. [Fox11](https://fox11online.com/news/health-news/green-bays-emplify-health-by-bellin-readies-for-possible-measles-patients-amid-case-surge)
- 2026-11-13: DHS reported a second pediatric death in Grant County and 649 cases in 20 counties since August.
  - Nearly 2,000 MMR doses have been delivered to local health departments since Aug 1.
  - More than 45,600 MMR doses have been given statewide in that period. [DHS release](https://www.dhs.wisconsin.gov/news/releases/111326.htm)
- 2026-11-13: Between Nov 10 and Nov 13, Grant, Iowa and Lafayette together went from 372 to 441 cases, and Jackson from 41 to 45. 14 people are hospitalized. [WIZM](https://www.wizmnews.com/2026/11/13/measles-case-reported-in-monroe-county-wi-at-551-cases/)
- Changes in the Nov 6 page snapshot versus Nov 13: [Wayback Nov 9](https://web.archive.org/web/20261109152026/https://www.dhs.wisconsin.gov/outbreaks/index.htm)

| Area | Nov 6 | Nov 13 |
|---|---|---|
| SW outbreak (Grant, Iowa, Lafayette, Vernon) | 376 | 455 |
| Jackson | 2 | 45 |
| Columbia | 33 | 47 |
| Green Lake | 5 | 14 |
| Marquette | 2 | 10 |

- 2026-11-05/06: First death (an infant) reported. A public exposure was flagged at the Marshfield Medical Center - Weston emergency department on Nov 5. [DHS RSS](https://www.dhs.wisconsin.gov/news/rss.xml)

### 4. Base rates and trend
Headline totals, with the average daily increase since the previous figure (background figures plus DHS pages):

| Date | Total | Cases per day |
|---|---|---|
| Sep 8 | 159 | |
| Sep 29 | 214 | about 2.6 |
| Oct 13 | 267 | about 3.8 |
| Oct 30 | 392 | about 7.4 |
| Nov 3 | 431 | about 9.8 |
| Nov 6 | 477 | about 15 |
| Nov 10 | 551 | about 18.5 |
| Nov 13 | 651 | about 33 |

- The daily increase has roughly doubled each week lately.
- Part of the Nov 10 to 13 jump may be reporting backlog. Jackson went from 2 to 41 in four days, 25 of those as probable cases.
- New clusters are still appearing in central Wisconsin (Columbia, Green Lake, Marquette, Jackson).
- DHS's page warns that newly reported counts "may vary" and that drops can reflect changes in how cases are found rather than real declines.

Simple straight-line projections from 651 over 14 days (Nov 13 to Nov 27):

| Pace assumed | Cases per day | Nov 27 total |
|---|---|---|
| Slowdown | 15 | about 860 |
| Nov 3 to 10 pace | 18 | about 900 |
| Nov 10 to 13 pace | 33 | about 1,110 |

If the Nov 27 update is not posted by 23:59 UTC, the Nov 24 figure counts instead, which is about 3 days less growth.

Seasonality and earlier years:
- There are no comparable earlier years. Wisconsin had 36 cases in all of 2025 and close to zero in most years before that, so there is no seasonal record to compare against for mid to late November.
- This year is far above any recent year.
- A comparison case is Pennsylvania's 2026 outbreak, which reached 1,542 cases across 46 counties. [Medscape](https://www.medscape.com/s/viewarticle/pennsylvania-wisconsin-report-measles-linked-deaths-cases-2026a10018fp)

### 5. Other forecasts
- I found no market or expert forecast on Wisconsin's count.
- Kalshi's US 2026 total market: "Above 7000" at 0.76, "Above 8000" at 0.21.
- Polymarket's US "by Nov 30" market: 6000+ at 0.55.
- These national markets are only loosely related.
- The CDC reported 5,412 US cases as of about Nov 12. [Latin Times](https://www.latintimes.com/paho-revokes-us-measles-elimination-status-601372)

### 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Expected DHS updates: Tue Nov 17 (not posted when I checked), Fri Nov 20, Tue Nov 24, Fri Nov 27.
- Thanksgiving (Thu Nov 26) is a state holiday. Holiday staffing could delay the Friday post past 23:59 UTC (5:59 pm CST).
- Holiday gatherings increase exposure, but measles takes 10 to 21 days to show symptoms, so cases from Thanksgiving contact would mostly be reported after the question resolves.
- Possible further DHS releases on exposures or deaths, and the effect of the vaccination push (45,600+ doses).
- Weather is not relevant.

## 4. Base rates and trend
Headline values (from the question background and the DHS page):
- Sept 8: 159; Sept 29: 214; Oct 13: 267; Oct 30: 392
- Nov 3: 431, then Nov 6: 477 (+46, about 15/day)

- Daily increases are still rising. If the pace stayed between 18 and 33 per day, the Nov 24 figure (about 11 days after Nov 13) would be roughly 850 to 1,010. A Nov 27 figure would be about 900 to 1,100. This is plain arithmetic, not a forecast.
- Some of the jump in new clusters (Columbia, Jackson) may come from batch reporting. DHS itself warns on the page that reported counts swing with case-finding phases, and that a fall in counts does not mean spread has slowed.
- Seasonality: there are no comparable earlier years. Wisconsin had 36 cases in all of 2025 and only isolated cases in 2021 to 2024, so there is no history for how counts move in the second half of November. The nearest comparison is the 2025 West Texas outbreak, where growth slowed about 2 to 3 months in. This outbreak is now about 3.5 months old (declared mid-August) but is still spreading to new counties.

Polymarket prices US cases of 6,000+ by Nov 30 at 0.55. The CDC reported 5,412 US cases as of about Nov 12. [Latin Times](https://www.latintimes.com/paho-revokes-us-measles-elimination-status-601372)

- Thanksgiving (Nov 26): fewer people seeking care and testing could hold counts down for a while, and travel and gatherings could cause cases later, but those would mostly appear after resolution because measles takes 10 to 21 days to show symptoms.
- Watch for more DHS-flagged exposure sites (for example the Weston emergency department) and further spread in Columbia, Jackson and Green Lake counties.
- Weather does not drive this outcome, so no forecast is included.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** About 10 days. The question resolves on whatever headline figure is on the DHS page at 23:59 UTC on Nov 27, 2026. That is likely the Fri Nov 27 update if it posts before 5:59 pm CST, and otherwise the Tue Nov 24 update. Thanksgiving week makes a late Friday post plausible, so I weight the two roughly equally, leaning slightly toward Friday.

(b) **Latest value:** 651 cases (headline "as of November 13, 2026"), still displayed on Nov 17.

(c) **If nothing changed:** 651. This is very unlikely given 3 to 4 more updates.

(d) **If the current trend continued:**
- The last week (Nov 6 to 13) added about 25 cases a day.
- The Nov 10 to 13 jump of about 33 a day was partly backlog: Jackson County went from 2 to 45 cases, 25 of them probable.
- At 25 cases a day, the total is about 925 by Nov 24 and about 1,000 by Nov 27.
- At the slower 15 to 18 a day pace, it is about 820 to 900.
- If growth keeps accelerating to 35 or more a day, it is about 1,100 to 1,150.

(e) **Historical variation:** Two-week increments have been rising: about 60 (late Sep), about 125 (Oct 13 to 30), and about 220 (Oct 30 to Nov 13). A 14-day increment of 200 to 450 is plausible, with clusters still seeding new counties.

(f) **Experts and markets:** There is no market on Wisconsin specifically. National markets (Kalshi above 7,000 for the year at 0.76) imply continued strong US growth, which is consistent with ongoing Wisconsin growth.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low:** The southwest outbreak burns out under reactive vaccination (45,600+ doses), the new clusters stay small, and the holiday-week reporting slows. In that case the Nov 24 update would show only about 750 to 780.
- **High:** The central Wisconsin clusters (Columbia, Green Lake, Marquette, Jackson) explode or a large case batch posts before Thanksgiving. Daily additions of 45 to 60 would push the total to 1,300 to 1,500.
